Only 1 and 2 therefore hold. Matches option A.

text: In the electrolytic refining of a metal M, what would you take as the anode, the cathode and the electrolyte?

options.text: Anode: Thin strip of pure metal (M); Cathode: Impure metal (M); Electrolyte: Distilled water
options.label: A

options.text: Anode: Impure metal (M); Cathode: Graphite rod; Electrolyte: Acid solution
options.label: B

options.text: Anode: Graphite rod; Cathode: Impure metal (M); Electrolyte: Molten salt of metal (M)
options.label: C

options.text: Anode: Impure metal (M); Cathode: thin strip of pure metal (M); Electrolyte: solution of a soluble salt of metal (M)
options.label: D

solution: In electrolytic refining the impure metal is made the anode, where it dissolves into the electrolyte, and a thin strip of the pure metal is the cathode, on which pure metal is deposited. The electrolyte must be a solution of a soluble salt of the same metal so that the metal ion concentration stays constant; the insoluble impurities settle below the anode as anode mud. Matches option D.

text: The decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is an example of
solution: Composting is the slow microbial oxidation of organic matter, in which the complex molecules are broken down and energy stored in them is released, which is why a compost heap becomes noticeably warm inside. A process that gives out heat is exothermic, and it does not involve an acid neutralising a base. Matches option C.

text: Which one of the following gases gives acidic solution on dissolving in water?
solution: Carbon dioxide is the acidic oxide of a non-metal and dissolves in water to give carbonic acid, \(\text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\), which turns blue litmus red and gives a pH below 7. Hydrogen, nitrogen and oxygen are essentially neutral gases and form no acid on dissolving in water. Matches option B.

text:
Consider the following statements about alloys:
1. Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.
2. Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.
3. Solder is an alloy of lead and tin.
4. Stainless Steel is an alloy of copper and chromium.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc, bronze is an alloy of copper and tin, and solder is an alloy of lead and tin used for joining electrical wires because of its low melting point, so statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: stainless steel is iron alloyed with chromium and nickel and contains no copper at all. Matches option A.

text: Which one of the following oxides dissolve in water?
solution: Sodium oxide is the oxide of a highly reactive alkali metal and dissolves readily in water to give a strongly alkaline solution, \(\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH}\). Copper oxide and \(\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\) are insoluble in water, and \(\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3\), although amphoteric, is also insoluble and dissolves only in acids and in strong alkalis. Matches option D.

text: Which one of the following is water gas?

options.text: Mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen
options.label: A

options.text: Mixture of carbon monoxide and nitrogen
options.label: B

options.text: Mixture of carbon dioxide and water vapour
options.label: C

options.text: Mixture of carbon monoxide and water vapour
options.label: D

solution: Water gas is the mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen produced by passing steam over red-hot coke, \(\text{C} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CO} + \text{H}_2\), and it is used as a fuel and as a source of hydrogen. The mixture of carbon monoxide and nitrogen obtained by blowing air over hot coke is producer gas, a different fuel gas. Matches option A.

text: Suppose you have four test tubes labelled A, B, C and D. A contains water, B contains solution of an alkali, C contains solution of an acid, and D contains solution of sodium chloride. Which one of these solutions will turn phenolphthalein solution pink?
solution: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic and neutral media and turns pink only in a basic medium, so only the alkali in tube B gives a pink colour. Water is neutral, sodium chloride solution is also neutral because \(\text{NaCl}\) is the salt of a strong acid and a strong base, and the acid in tube C leaves the indicator colourless. Matches option B.

text: Which among the following are essential constituents of Portland cement?
solution: Portland cement is made by strongly heating a mixture that supplies lime (\(\text{CaO}\), from limestone), silica (\(\text{SiO}_2\)) and alumina (\(\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3\), from clay), together with small amounts of iron oxide, the clinker then being ground with gypsum. Graphite and graphene play no part in cement manufacture, and sand alone does not supply the alumina and lime needed. Matches option B.

text: Galvanization is a method of protecting iron from rusting by coating with a thin layer of:
solution: Galvanisation is the deposition of a thin layer of zinc on iron or steel, usually by hot dipping or electroplating. Zinc is more reactive than iron, so besides sealing the surface it acts as a sacrificial coating and corrodes preferentially, protecting the iron even where the layer is scratched. Matches option C.

text: Consider the following reaction: Fe2O3(s) + 2Al(s) -> 2Fe(s) + Al2O3(s) Which of the following statements about the given reaction is NOT correct?

options.text: It is an example of displacement reaction
options.label: A

options.text: This reaction helps in joining of railway tracks
options.label: D

solution: The thermite reaction \(\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 + 2\text{Al} \rightarrow 2\text{Fe} + \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3\) is a displacement in which aluminium reduces the iron oxide, so \(\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\) is the oxidising agent and the molten iron produced is used to weld railway tracks and cracked machine parts. It liberates a very large amount of heat, that is it is highly exothermic, so describing it as endothermic is the statement that is not correct. Matches option B.

text: Consider the following reaction: (heat) 2HgO ----------> 2Hg + O2 ( room temperature) The respective state of HgO, Hg and O2 in the above reaction is
solution: Mercuric oxide, \(\text{HgO}\), is an orange-red solid that decomposes on heating. The mercury set free is a liquid at room temperature, mercury being the only metal that is liquid under ordinary conditions, and oxygen is evolved as a gas. Matches option B.

text: Kerosene and petrol mixture can be best separated by:
solution: Kerosene and petrol are miscible petroleum fractions whose boiling ranges differ but are fairly close, so they are separated by fractional distillation, in which a fractionating column provides repeated cycles of vaporisation and condensation. A separating funnel works only for immiscible liquids, and sublimation applies only to solids that vaporise directly. Matches option C.

text: Which one of the following metals floats in cold water?
solution: Calcium reacts with cold water at a moderate rate and the bubbles of hydrogen produced cling to the surface of the metal, so the piece of calcium floats on the water. Magnesium reacts only very slowly with cold water, copper does not react at all, and potassium reacts so violently that the hydrogen catches fire at once rather than simply buoying the metal up. Matches option B.

text: Which of the following statements is not true about Carbon compounds?

options.text: Diamond has a trihedral structure and is the hardest material known to man
options.label: A

options.text: Buckminster Fullerene is also a carbon compound with 60 carbon atoms
options.label: B

options.text: Graphite has a hexagonal layered structure, and each carbon is bonded via a strong covalent bond
options.label: C

options.text: Graphite is a good conductor of electricity due to delocalised electrons
options.label: D

solution: In diamond each carbon atom is covalently bonded to four others in a rigid three-dimensional tetrahedral network, not a trihedral structure, so statement A is the untrue one. The other three are correct: buckminsterfullerene is \(\text{C}_{60}\), graphite is built of hexagonal layers of covalently bonded carbon atoms, and the fourth electron of each carbon in graphite is delocalised, which makes graphite a good conductor. Matches option A.

text: During whitewashing of walls, which of the following reactions take place: i. CaO(s)+CO2(aq) --- CaCO3(s) ii. CaCO3(s)+H2O(l)----Ca(OH)2 + CO2 iii. CaO(s)+H2O(l)-------Ca(OH)2(aq) iv. Ca(OH)2(aq)+CO2(g)-----CaCO3(s)+H2O(l)
solution: Whitewashing begins with quicklime slaked in water, \(\text{CaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2\), and the slaked lime suspension is applied to the wall. It then slowly absorbs carbon dioxide from the air, \(\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\), and the thin film of calcium carbonate formed gives the hard shiny white finish, so step iii is followed by step iv. Matches option B.
